title: Configured printers
whyItMatters: CUPS lists every printer the machine can reach, with its queue name and often a network address or a saved SMB/Windows login. It tells a stranger which office, home or print shop the person used, and how to reach those devices.
source: printers.conf(5): CUPS keeps the printer definitions in /etc/cups/printers.conf, readable only by root and the lp group: https://man.archlinux.org/man/printers.conf.5
notes: Normally root-only, so requiresElevation. Device URIs can embed smb:// or ipp:// addresses, and some embed credentials for a Windows print share. Printers added only in the desktop settings without running cupsd are not listed here.

steps: Open Settings > Printers from your desktop environment.
Click the options menu next to each configured printer and select Remove Printer.
An administrator password may be required.
cleanup.risk: Removes all configured local and network printers. You will need to reconfigure printer drivers and queues to print again. Printers added by other users on this machine go too.
cleanup.source: GNOME Help, Set up a local printer: https://help.gnome.org/users/gnome-help/stable/printing-setup.html
